Any order of the n edge-transpositions along the path is one (n+1)-cycle. A global translation puts the affine map on constant-sum hyperplane H_c, whose c=0 is equivalent to solvability of A(P_n)x=b; the odd-n kernel is the alternating vector. P^t fixes gcd(t,n+1) cycles and one affine sum constraint yields the displayed counts; primitive period witnesses and Möbius inversion establish support and exact order. Independent exhaustive GF2/GF4 checks covered 4696 offset/order instances, not the all-n proof.
